originality.rationale: The published source establishes the model, conditional Gaussian description and t^-1/2 moment decay, not a fixed-displacement rare-excursion intensity. A closer earlier result for Brownian-power stiffness proves the Cauchy weak limit of sqrt(t)X at power two, but does not imply a fixed-u order-t^-1/2 asymptotic; taking a growing threshold inside a weak limit is not justified. The matching small-u coefficient alone is acknowledged as subsumed. The contribution is the full intensity measure and exact positive fixed-u exceedance function with a justified sequential inner boundary.

value.rationale: Provides an entire fixed-displacement rare-excursion intensity (not an arbitrary higher moment), its sharp universal singular near-origin law, and the bridge between Cauchy-scale typical fluctuations and probability of physically macroscopic displacements. These quantities can inform threshold-sensitive measurements even when all low-order moments collapse as t^-1/2. A full distribution-level limit is a natural missing observable not supplied by moment asymptotics.
